key_insight: Data-informed random features provide a compact dictionary for learning continuous-time nonlinear dynamics through Koopman generator approximations.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports forecasting and system analysis with interpretable linear-operator models while reducing reliance on iterative optimization.
method: Construct a data-informed random-feature representation of observables.
Approximate the Koopman generator using Galerkin methods such as gEDMD.
Establish convergence of reconstructed vector fields and trajectories.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments demonstrate accurate forecasting and system analysis, with faster computation than iterative optimization, though the abstract gives no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: gEDMD does not generally preserve exponential boundedness, so stability of the learned evolution requires careful assessment.
paper_title: Data-driven Random-feature Approximation of Koopman Generators of Nonlinear Continuous-time Systems
